## Why Sequences Matter

**Classical RecSys Assumption:**
Users' preferences are **static** and **independent**

**Reality:**
Users consume items in **sequences** with **temporal dynamics**

::: {.fragment}
```text
Alice watches:
Toy Story → Finding Nemo → Up → Inside Out

Next recommendation?
→ Probably another Pixar film!
→ NOT just "similar to any one film"
```
:::

---

## Sequential Patterns

**Session-based behavior:**

```text
[Action] → [Action] → [Comedy]
               ↓
         Mood shift!
```

**Topic evolution:**

```text
[Star Wars I] → [Star Wars II] → [Star Wars III]
                       ↓
                 Binge watching
```

**Temporal context:**

```text
Weekend evening → likely wants entertainment
Tuesday morning → maybe documentary
```

---

## Beyond Item-Item Similarity

**Item-item CF:**
- "Users who liked A also liked B"
- Ignores **order** and **recency**

**Sequential modeling:**
- "After watching [A, B, C], users watch D"
- Captures **temporal patterns**
- Models **short-term intent**

::: {.fragment}
**Examples:**
- Markov Chains
- RNNs / LSTMs
- **Transformers** ← Today's focus!
:::

---

## Enter the Transformer

**Original use case**: Neural Machine Translation

```text
Source: "How are you?"
        ↓
   [Transformer]
        ↓
Target: "Comment allez-vous?"
```

**Key innovation**: Self-attention mechanism

---

## Self-Attention Intuition

**Traditional RNN**: Process sequence left-to-right, one step at a time

**Transformer**: All positions attend to all other positions **simultaneously**

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Input Sequence:**
```text
[Toy Story]
[Finding Nemo]
[Up]
[?]
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Attention:**
```text
[?] looks at:
  - Toy Story (weight: 0.3)
  - Finding Nemo (weight: 0.4)  
  - Up (weight: 0.5)
```

Learns to focus on **relevant** history!
:::
:::

---

## Self-Attention Formula

$$
\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d}}\right) V
$$

Where:
- **Q** (Query): "What am I looking for?"
- **K** (Key): "What do I contain?"
- **V** (Value): "What information do I carry?"

::: {.fragment}
**For recommendation:**
- Input: sequence of item embeddings
- Output: contextualized representations
- Each item embedding is informed by **all previous items**
:::

---

## Causal Masking

**Problem**: At training time, we can see the future!

**Solution**: Mask future positions

```text
Input:    [A]  [B]  [C]  [D]
           ↓    ↓    ↓    ↓
Predict:  [B]  [C]  [D]  [?]

When predicting C:
  ✓ Can attend to A, B
  ✗ Cannot attend to C, D
```

::: {.fragment}
Creates **autoregressive** next-item prediction!
:::

---

## Attention Matrix Visualization

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Causal attention mask
seq_len = 5
mask = np.tril(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)))

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 5))
plt.imshow(mask, cmap='Blues', aspect='auto')
plt.xlabel('Key Position')
plt.ylabel('Query Position')
plt.title('Causal Attention Mask')
plt.xticks(range(seq_len), ['Item 1', 'Item 2', 'Item 3', 'Item 4', 'Item 5'])
plt.yticks(range(seq_len), ['Item 1', 'Item 2', 'Item 3', 'Item 4', 'Item 5'])

for i in range(seq_len):
    for j in range(seq_len):
        if mask[i, j]:
            plt.text(j, i, '✓', ha='center', va='center', color='white', fontsize=16)
        else:
            plt.text(j, i, '✗', ha='center', va='center', color='gray', fontsize=16)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

---

## Positional Encodings

**Problem**: Attention is permutation-invariant!

[A, B, C] and [C, B, A] look the same without position info.

**Solution**: Add positional embeddings

$$
\text{Input}_i = \text{ItemEmb}_i + \text{PosEmb}_i
$$

Tells the model: "Item X appeared at position T in the sequence"

```{mermaid}
    Add1 --> FFN[Feed-Forward Network]
    FFN --> Add2[Add & Normalize]
    Add1 --> Add2
    Add2 --> Output[Output]

```

Stack multiple blocks for deeper models!

---

## SASRec: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation

**Paper**: Kang & McAuley (2018), ICDM

**Key ideas:**
- Apply transformers to recommendation
- Causal self-attention over item sequences
- Next-item prediction objective

**Architecture:**
1. Item embeddings + positional embeddings
2. 2-4 transformer blocks
3. Predict next item from final hidden state

---

## SASRec vs. Traditional Methods

| **Aspect**              | **Matrix Factorization** | **SASRec**                     |
|-------------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Input                   | User-item pairs          | Item sequences                 |
| Temporal modeling       | ✗                        | ✓                              |
| User representation     | Static embedding         | Dynamic (from sequence)        |
| Context window          | N/A                      | Last N items                   |
| Captures short-term     | ✗                        | ✓                              |

---

## Training Objective

**Next-item prediction:**

Given sequence: $[i_1, i_2, ..., i_t]$

Predict: $i_{t+1}$

**Loss function:**

$$
\mathcal{L} = -\sum_{t=1}^{T} \log P(i_{t+1} | i_1, ..., i_t)
$$

Cross-entropy loss over item vocabulary!

---

## Evaluation Metrics

**Ranking metrics:**

- **Recall@K**: Are relevant items in top-K?
- **NDCG@K**: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (position matters!)
- **MRR**: Mean Reciprocal Rank

**Evaluation protocol:**
- Hold out last N interactions per user
- Predict next items
- Measure ranking quality

---

## Why Transformers Win

**Pros:**
- Capture long-range dependencies
- Parallel training (faster than RNNs)
- State-of-the-art performance

**Cons:**
- More parameters than EASE
- Requires more data
- Harder to interpret

::: {.fragment}
**Trade-off**: Complexity vs. performance

For large catalogs with rich sequential data → Transformers shine!
:::

---

## Key Papers: Sequential RecSys

**RNN-based:**
- Hidasi et al., "Session-based Recommendations with RNNs" (2016)

**Transformer-based:**
- Kang & McAuley, "Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (SASRec)" (2018) ← **Today**
- Sun et al., "BERT4Rec" (2019) - Bidirectional variant

**Foundations:**
- Vaswani et al., "Attention Is All You Need" (2017) - Original transformer
